messages.text: Our office espresso machine is leaking. A wants a simpler one and B wants to keep the old one. I don't want a fight over coffee. Can you help us sort it out?

I’d mainly hope for something simple and low-maintenance, so it’s easy to use day to day. I’m a little worried about taking on repairs, a cleaning rota, or lots of back-and-forth, especially after long days.
Something else: it was our dad’s, and I want to keep it going. It’s wearing me down, though, so any repair talk needs to fit into short slots.
That seems workable if you both agree on the limits beforehand. I can’t take on coordinating the repair, and I hadn’t known it was your dad’s.

I understand why B wants to preserve it. A one-time check with clear limits sounds reasonable, but I’m afraid I can’t arrange it; I don’t have the energy to coordinate repairs. If someone else can handle it, we could agree a cost cap and deadline first, then replace it if either limit is exceeded.
Yes, I’d accept one check and replace it if the repair isn’t worthwhile. I can’t give a cost cap without knowing the repair; let’s agree one before the check, and keep the check to a short slot.
I don’t know who else could call. If B is willing, that sounds workable; the cost cap and deadline still need agreement. I can share them once you’ve settled them.
Yes, I can make one short call for a quote. No work starts until we’ve agreed the cap and deadline.

That sounds workable in principle, and I appreciate B making the call. I can review the quote and settle a cap and deadline with her in one brief exchange; if we can’t agree quickly, let’s replace it. The figures aren’t decided yet.
Good. I’ll make the call and share the quote; no work starts before we agree on the limits.
Yes. Once A and B agree on the cap and deadline, send them to me and I’ll share them with everyone.
Fine. Once I have the quote and A has reviewed it, I’ll agree the limits with her and send them to C.
